# Risk model card

**Model:** `fraud-gbm-v1` — LightGBM gradient-boosted trees; isotonic calibration. Trained 2026-09-30 in 13.5 s. Generated by `uv run python -m ml.model_card`.

## Intended use

Scores payments in the Tally *simulation* before authorization. The score is combined with versioned rules; the model can allow, send to review or step-up, or block. It is not validated on real payment data and must not be used for real decisions.

## Data

- Synthetic events from `ml/datagen.py` (seed 7, 60 days, 20,000 customers): legitimate spending with look-alike behaviour (micro-payment bursts, one-off large payments to new payees, travel, device changes) and three fraud patterns (card testing, account takeover including on the victim's own device, mule fan-in). Labels include noise: 3% of fraud unreported and 0.05% friendly fraud.
- Split by time — train first 2/3 of days, validate next 1/6, test last 1/6 — so validation and test are strictly after training. Rows: train 186,734, validation 46,556, test 46,568; test fraud rate 0.85%.
- Features (19) are computed by `services/risk/features.py`, the same code the service uses online; `tests/integration/test_risk_feature_parity.py` checks identical vectors from Redis and offline replay.

## Performance (held-out test window)

| Metric | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| PR-AUC (average precision) | 0.8881 |
| ROC-AUC | 0.9785 |
| Recall / precision at 0.1% FPR | 89.09% / 88.41% |
| Recall / precision at 1% FPR | 92.13% / 44.05% |
| Brier score (calibrated) | 0.00157 |
| Expected calibration error | 0.00040 |
| ONNX vs LightGBM max score difference | 8.8e-08 |

### Operating thresholds (chosen on validation by cost)

Missed fraud costs its amount; a review costs ₹25; a wrongly blocked payment costs ₹250. The review threshold (0.0060) minimises validation cost; the block threshold (0.9730) is the lowest at or above it with validation precision ≥ 90.00%.

| At threshold | Recall | Precision |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Review / step-up | 93.65% | 25.86% |
| Block | 78.43% | 95.37% |

False-positive rate at the review threshold: 2.29%. Test-window cost: ₹124,903 with the model vs ₹3,527,969 of fraud with no screening.

Recall by fraud pattern at the review threshold: card_testing 99.56%, account_takeover 93.10%, mule 99.01%.

Rules only (default rule set, no model): recall 42.13%, precision 22.13%, false-positive rate 1.26%.

## Explainability

Every decision stores its top three positive TreeSHAP contributions (LightGBM `pred_contrib`, exact for trees) mapped to reason codes such as `DEVICE_MANY_CARDS`, `NEW_DEVICE` or `AMOUNT_VS_HISTORY`, alongside the rule reasons.

## Fairness and subgroup notes

Legitimate customers whose IP country differs from their account country (travellers, non-resident Indians; 480 test rows) are flagged at 15.21% versus 2.16% for customers at home. This is a material disparity: `geo_mismatch` is predictive in the synthetic data but correlates with nationality and residence. Mitigations before any real use: step-up instead of block for this segment, monitor the per-segment false-positive rate, and consider removing or constraining the feature. No protected attributes are used directly; the synthetic data cannot measure outcomes by gender, religion, caste or age.

## Monitoring and lifecycle

- Drift: PSI and KS per feature and on the score against the training baselines stored in `metadata.json` (`POST /v1/drift/run`); PSI ≥ 0.2 is an alert.
- Feedback: chargebacks and analyst review outcomes become `risk_labels` joined to the logged feature vectors; `ml/retrain.py` retrains, registers the candidate and makes it the shadow challenger only if it passes the evaluation gate (PR-AUC and recall at 1% FPR within 0.02 of the champion, ONNX parity). Champion promotion needs maker-checker.
- Serving: ONNX Runtime score + LightGBM TreeSHAP; in-process decision latency measured in `tests/integration/test_risk_flow.py` (see PROGRESS for the latest numbers).

## Limits

- The generator and model were built together; real fraud is adaptive and far less separable. Treat these metrics as a test of the pipeline, not of fraud performance.
- Calibration is isotonic on one validation window; it will drift with base rates.
